tools.name: SendPenDown
tools.description: Tell STP that the user has started a sketch stroke (pen or mouse down) at a map coordinate. Send it once at the start of each stroke, then send the whole stroke with SendInk when the pen lifts. Fire and forget: the engine sends no reply and no event. A missing location or a malformed timestamp is silently ignored.

tools.name: SendInk
tools.description: Send one sketched stroke for recognition, when the pen lifts (after SendPenDown). Use it to turn what a user draws, alone or with speech sent at about the same time (SendSpeechRecognition or SendSimulatedSpeechRecognition), into symbols, tasks, edits or commands; to place a fully specified symbol without recognition, use AddSymbol instead. List in intersectedPoids the symbols the stroke crosses, so the gesture can move, edit or delete them. Recognition starts when the segmentation timeout expires (see ChangeTimeOut) or on RecognizeNow. Fire and forget: the engine sends no reply; the outcome arrives only as the events listed - InkProcessed when the sketch is finished, then SymbolAdded, TaskAdded and so on if it was recognized, or nothing more if it was not. A sketch that is not recognized is discarded and still sends InkProcessed, which can come several seconds later (about 10 s in the capture); engines before STP-1080 send none for it. A missing strokePoints or a malformed time is refused with an StpMessage (engines before STP-1088 ignore it silently).

tools.name: SendSpeechRecognition
tools.description: Send a speech recognizer's hypotheses for one utterance (an n-best list of text with confidence). STP fuses speech with ink sent at about the same time (SendInk) to create or edit symbols and tasks; speech alone can also do that, or be a command. For typed text use SendSimulatedSpeechRecognition, which converts numbers and letters to spoken form. Fire and forget: the engine sends no reply. SpeechParsed (to the caller) follows with the hypotheses that matched the grammar, SpeechRecognized carries the single phrase that integrated, and any symbol or task arrives as the events listed. An empty or missing recoList, or a malformed time, is silently ignored.

tools.name: SendSimulatedSpeechRecognition
tools.description: Send typed text as if a speech recognizer had heard it - the simplest way for a program to 'say' a phrase such as 'infantry platoon', with a SendInk stroke or on its own. Numbers and letters are converted server-side to spoken form (e.g. 'A 3 1' becomes 'alpha three one'); startTime defaults to now and the utterance is taken to last 0.5 s. Fire and forget: the engine sends no reply. SpeechParsed (to the caller) always follows, SpeechRecognized carries the phrase that integrated, and a recognized symbol or task arrives as SymbolAdded / TaskAdded. Text the grammar does not match gives SpeechParsed with no alternates and nothing else; missing text is silently ignored.

tools.name: GetScenarioContent
tools.description: Return the whole current scenario as object_set([...]) text - the form to save a plan and later restore it with LoadNewScenario (replace) or ImportPlanData / SyncScenarioSession (merge). It holds the planning scenario, COAs, symbols, tasks and task orgs, plus deleted objects carrying the deletion version; session state such as viewports and ink is left out. tools.name: JoinScenarioSession

Task orgs themselves are not replayed (no TaskOrgAdded): list them with GetScenarioTaskOrgList. Changes nothing on the server. Call it after connecting to a session whose scenario already exists; to also merge content of your own, use SyncScenarioSession. Answers null; with no scenario it still succeeds. Engines before STP-1083 fail it after an UndoLastOp that undid an add.

tools.name: SyncScenarioSession

tools.name: AddSymbol

The engine assigns the poid and fills in the descriptions from the sidc. Fire and forget: the engine sends no reply; the result arrives as SymbolAdded (to every client, with the new poid), after an InkProcessed to the caller. A symbol without a valid sidc and location produces only InkProcessed and no symbol; a missing symbol is silently ignored. Needs an active scenario: with none the symbol is still created, but HasActiveScenario stays false.

tools.name: ConvertC2SIMContent
tools.description: Convert a C2SIM XML document (for example an Initialization from PullC2SIMInitialization) into STP object_set([...]) text. The conversion is local to the engine: nothing is loaded into the scenario and no C2SIM server is contacted, so options is ignored. Know three things before relying on the result. SYMBOLS ONLY: units and tactical graphics are converted, tasks are not - STP tasks carry more detail than C2SIM captures. NOT IDEMPOTENT: every call mints task orgs to hold the symbols (one per affiliation present, named 'Friendly TO' and 'Hostile TO') with fresh poids, so converting the same document twice yields two different task orgs. NO PARENT COA: no COA is minted and no object carries a parent COA; a caller that needs COA-parented objects, to load them into a scenario say, must mint the COAs and parent the objects itself. Well-formed XML with nothing convertible returns an empty object_set([]); malformed XML or missing content is refused.

That is deliberate, and it differs from the sibling C2SIM methods on purpose: those carry an enumerated key set and reject an unknown key rather than ignoring it (STP-687), whereas this method has no key set to enumerate. Those keys configure the C2SIM bridge agent, and this conversion is purely local to the engine's SDK layer and never reaches that agent. Nothing passed here can change the result.

Read-only: nothing changes in STP and nothing is sent - use PushC2SIMContent to send a document to a C2SIM server. Refused when there is nothing to export: no units, graphics or task org items for Initialization (as in a session with no scenario), or no confirmed tasks for Order (see ConfirmTask).

tools.name: RecognizeNow
tools.description: Recognize the strokes collected so far now, instead of waiting for the segmentation timeout to expire - useful when the timeout is long (ChangeTimeOut) and the user has finished drawing. Fire and forget: the engine sends no reply; the result arrives as the events listed (InkProcessed, then SymbolAdded and so on). Strokes that are not recognized are discarded and still send InkProcessed, which can come several seconds later (about 10 s in the capture); engines before STP-1080 send none for them. With nothing pending it does nothing and sends nothing.

tools.name: SendListen
tools.description: Start or stop STP's speech listening: mode once listens until the first inactivity, on until told to stop, off stops. Compared with SetSpeechListening (on/off), it adds the once mode and a timestamp. mode may be sent as the name or as its ordinal (0, 1, 2); the .NET SDK sends the ordinal. Fire and forget; no event reports the state, and a missing or unknown mode is silently ignored.

mode.description: Listening mode: once (0) listens until the first inactivity, on (1) listens until told to stop, off (2) stops.

time.description: Timestamp of the request. Defaults to now.

tools.name: SendAudioCaptureState
tools.description: Report whether this client is currently capturing audio, so other components can reflect it in their user interface. It reports state only; use SetSpeechListening or SendListen to control listening. Fire and forget; no event follows, and a missing isListening is silently ignored.

isListening.description: True while this client is capturing audio.

tools.name: AdvertiseViewport
tools.description: Tell STP which map area this client is showing: topLeft is the north-west corner and botRight the south-east corner. STP keeps it as the context for this client's strokes; SendInk sends its own map extents the same way when they change, so call this when the view moves without a stroke. Fire and forget; no event follows, and a missing corner is silently ignored.

topLeft.description: North-west corner of the visible map.

botRight.description: South-east corner of the visible map.

tools.name: SetAutoTasking
tools.description: Turn automatic (implicit) tasking on or off: when on, STP infers tasks from the symbols placed, without an explicitly spoken task, and announces them with TaskAdded (taskStatus implicit). Scenario loads and merges (LoadNewScenario, ImportPlanData, SyncScenarioSession) suspend it while they run and restore it afterwards. Fire and forget; no event confirms the setting, and a missing isEnabled is silently ignored.

tools.name: ResetRole
tools.description: Clear this client's role, leaving it with no role - the same as SetRole with 'none', without waiting for confirmation. Fire and forget: the engine sends no reply; RoleSwitched with a null role follows if a role was set, and CoaSwitched / TaskOrgSwitched if the client's current COA or task org changes with it.

stp/emits.condition: a role was set (RoleSwitched with no role)
the caller's current COA changes with the role

tools.name: UndoLastOp
tools.description: Undo the last operation applied to one object - a symbol, task, task org unit or relationship - identified by poid. STP replays the effect to every client in the session as ordinary events carrying isUndo = true - *Deleted for an undone add, *Modified with the previous state for an undone change, *Added for an undone delete - so a client that already handles the Added/Modified/Deleted events needs no extra handling. Each call undoes one operation; call it again to go further back. AddTask is followed at once by a change to the task, so undoing a task add takes two calls (TaskModified, then TaskDeleted). Fire and forget. An unknown or missing poid is silently ignored. Engines before STP-1080 send no event for an undo (read the object back with GetPoidObject), and engines before STP-1083 fail JoinScenarioSession and GetScenarioContent after an undone add.

poid.description: Unique id of the object whose last operation is to be undone.

tools.name: ResetStpScenario
tools.description: Discard the whole scenario - every object and the planning scenario itself - leaving the session with no active scenario (HasActiveScenario answers false) until CreateNewScenario or LoadNewScenario. It also clears the current COA (CoaSwitched with no COA) and the default task orgs. Returns no value. No Deleted event is sent per object; other clients of the session receive NewScenario, the caller does not. With no scenario left, a second call does nothing.

tools.name: GetActiveScenarioDescription
tools.description: Return the planning scenario object of the current scenario - its Name, poid and flags such as IsLoaded - without any of its contents, or null when the session has no active scenario. HasActiveScenario answers just the yes/no. Read-only.

tools.name: GetAllObjects
tools.description: Return every live object in the session as a flat JSON array - planning scenario, COAs, symbols, tasks, task orgs with their units and relationships, plus session-state objects such as system_state; deleted objects are not included (see GetDeletedObjects). Each object carries fsTYPE, poid, timestamps and version, with its content in PrologTerm as STP text (10 objects came to about 8.5 KB; engines before STP-1090 send PrologTerm as a much larger nested array, about 2 MB for 50 objects). Prefer GetScenarioContent for the scenario, GetPoidObject for one object and GetScenarioTaskOrgList for task orgs. Read-only.

tools.name: GetDeletedObjects
tools.description: Return the objects deleted from the current scenario. A deleted object is TOMBSTONED rather than removed (dbVersion v0), so it is still listed here; use it to confirm a delete whose event did not arrive. Same object shape as GetAllObjects (content in PrologTerm). Read-only; [] with no scenario.

tools.name: GetPoidObject
tools.description: Return one object of any type (symbol, task, COA, task org, unit or relationship) by its unique id, as fsTYPE, poid, timestamps, version and its content in PrologTerm; null when no object carries that poid. Use it to check the outcome of a fire-and-forget call whose event did not arrive. Read-only. A missing poid returns the session's system_state object instead of null, so always send one.

poid.description: Unique id of the object to fetch.

tools.name: GetScenarioTaskOrgList
tools.description: Return the task organizations (ORBATs) defined in the current scenario as summaries - poid, name, affiliation and timestamp - newest first, without their units. This is where to find TO poids for SetCoaTaskOrg, GetTaskOrgContent and parentTO in AddTaskOrgUnit; JoinScenarioSession does not replay TaskOrgAdded. Read-only; [] with no scenario.

tools.name: GetTaskOrgObjects
tools.description: Return the objects making up a task organization (the task_org with its units and relationships) as a plain array. This is a SYNONYM of GetTaskOrgObjectSet - both reach the same engine call and return the same array; the two spellings exist because the .NET SDK grew both. Each object carries its content in PrologTerm, as STP text; the array is valid input for ImportTaskOrgFromObjectSet as it is (engines before STP-1090 return a nested array that no import reads back). Read-only. An unknown poid returns []; a missing poid returns every object in the session.
